html:
The Yaminawá are a Panoan people of the borderlands of Acre in Brazil, Madre de Dios in Peru and Pando in Bolivia. Their home region is Acre.

They live along rivers in the forest by hunting, fishing and farming. The rubber boom of around 1900 brought violence, forced labour and disease, and many groups split and moved. Yaminawá is also used loosely for several closely related Panoan groups. Neighbours and kin include the Sharanahua, the Huni Kuin, the Amahuaca and the Nawa.
